title: Coroner's inquest called into 2017 death of Cambridge man
subtitle: CAMBRIDGE - The 2017 death of a Cambridge man will be examined by a coroner's inquest.
article: The 2017 death of a Cambridge man will be examined by a coroner's inquest.

On May 22, 2017, Kieran Kay, 26, was pronounced dead in hospital while in custody of the Waterloo Regional Police Service. An inquest, which is mandatory under the Coroners Act, will examine the circumstances of Kay's death and a jury will make recommendations aimed at preventing similar deaths.

Ontario's Special Investigations Unit, which carries out investigations into serious police-involved situations that result in injury or death, cleared a Waterloo Regional police officer of wrongdoing in the case early last year. A toxicology report found that Kay died as a result of acute cocaine toxicity.
A date for the coroner's inquest has not yet been scheduled.
